units.slavonic_text: *) Утреня воскресная Недѣли Пасхи есть туй въ своей полнотѣ сложенна. **) Вел. Святый и „Нарочитымъ“ называется.
units.english_text: 3. The Triodion (in Greek: *Triodion* [Τριῴδιον], from the words: *treis ode* [τρεῖς ᾠδή] = *tres odae*, *liber trium odarum* [three odes, book of three odes]). It is called “Triodion” because the canon of daily Matins in the Great Fast for the most part consisteth not of 9, but only of three odes. Besides this, on a certain day the canon hath only two odes, and such is called a “Diodion” [*Dvopesnets*], and yet on another four, and such is called a “Tetraodion” [*Chetyrepesnets*].[^35] The Triodion containeth in itself services both Sunday and weekday, namely from the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee even unto Great Saturday; certain newer Ruthenian editions, however, have it only up to Lazarus Saturday. For Sunday services it hath: (α) Vespers stichera; (β) At Matins the stichera sung after Psalm 50 in place of “Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ,” namely at “Glory”: “Open unto me the doors of repentance,” at “Now and ever”: “Guide me into the paths of salvation”; (γ) It hath one ca- non.[^36] (δ) The exaposteilarion sung after the 9th ode. (ε) Two stichera at the Praises and at “Glory.” For weekday services it hath: (α) At Vespers three stichera and two readings, and stichera at the aposticha. (β) Small Matins with three sessional hymns and with three odes of the canon. (γ) The Triadicon exaposteilarion with “Glory,” which is read only after the 9th ode. (δ) At the end it hath a small Typikon. It must be noted that this book in the Greek-Ruthenian Church is also called the “Lenten Triodion.”

units.english_text: 4. The Pentecostarion, that is, the book (in Greek: *Pentecostarion* [Πεντηκοστάριον], from the word: *pentekonta* [πεντήκοντα] = *quinquaginta* [fifty]). It containeth in itself all services from the Sunday of Pascha (in Ruthenian editions from Lazarus Saturday) unto the Sunday of All Saints. For daily divine services: regular Vespers on 3 stichera, Matins with two kathismata and sessional hymns, the Sunday canon, and stichera at the aposticha.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 4 пятдесятничька т е книга по гречески
units.slavonic_text: 4. Пятдесятничька т. е. книга, (по гречески: „Πεντηκοστάριον“ отъ слова: „πεντήκοντα“ == quinquaginta). Содержитъ въ себѣ всѣ отправы отъ Недѣли Пасхи, (оу рѹсскихъ изданіяхъ отъ Сѹбботы Лазаревой), до Недѣли Всѣхъ Святыхъ. И то α) Отправы страстной седмицы. β) Отправы свѣтлой седмицы. γ) Отправы отъ Антипасхи до Недѣли Всѣхъ Святыхъ. На недѣлныя Богослѹженія: Вечерню съ стихирами воскресными и съ стихирами на стиховнѣхъ. Оутреню съ сѣдальными, канонъ воскресенъ съ свѣтильнымъ и стихиры на „Хвалите“-хъ. На Богослѹженія дневныя: Вечерню порядочнѹю на 3 стихи, Оутреню съ двѣма каѳизмами и сѣдальными, канонъ воскресенъ и стихиры на стиховнѣхъ.
units.english_text: 5. The Octoechos (in Greek: *Octoechos* [Ὀκτώηχος], from the words: *octo* [ὀκτώ] and *echos* [ἦχος] = *octo* et *sonus* [eight and tone/sound]). It beginneth on the Sunday of All Saints in the evening and is used alone until the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee, and together with the Triodion until Lazarus Saturday. It containeth in itself: Sunday and weekday services according to the 8 tones, and that in each tone: (α) The Sunday service, namely: stichera of Small and Great Vespers, both at “Lord, I have cried” and at the aposticha; furthermore, the Theotokion canon of Compline, the Trinity canon of the Midnight Office, sessional hymns, the hypakoe, the morning graduals [stepenny], a threefold Matins canon: of the Resurrection, Cross-Resurrection, and Theotokion, Sunday stichera at the Praises, and the Beatitudes at the Liturgy; (β) The Monday service: Vespers with stichera, the Theotokion canon of Compline, Matins with 3 sessional hymns and with two canons, namely: of Repentance and to the Angels, stichera at the aposticha, and the Beatitudes; (γ) The Tuesday service: It containeth in itself the stichera of Vespers, the Theotokion canon of Compline, and Matins with sessional hymns and with two canons, namely: of Repentance and to the Forerunner; (δ) The Wednesday service: It containeth in itself: evening stichera, the Theotokion canon of Compline, and Matins with sessional hymns and with two canons, namely: of the Theotokos and of the Cross; (ε) The Thursday service: It containeth in itself: evening stichera, the Theotokion canon of Compline, and Matins with sessional hymns and with two canons: to the Holy Apostles and to St. Nicholas; (ϛ) The Friday service, that is, stichera of the Cross and Stavrotheotokia at Vespers, the canon of the Theotokos at Compline, at Matins after the sessional hymns the canon: of the Cross and of the Theotokos; (η) The Saturday service: It containeth in itself: evening stichera, the Theotokion canon of Compline, and Matins with sessional hymns and with two canons: to All Saints and for the Departed. At the Praises (which the other days do not have) martyr stichera, and at the aposticha stichera for the departed. Besides these, there are found here: (ϑ) The Triadica of Gregory of Sinai used on Sunday at the Midnight Office after the Theotokion canon; (ι) Troparia after the Evlogitaria [Amomos / Psalm 118]: “The angelic council,” etc.; (κ) The 11 Matins Gospels with 11 Sunday exaposteilaria and with 11 Gospel stichera; (λ) Daily exaposteilaria sung throughout the entire week, and daily Triadica for the Holy Forty Days; (μ) A small Typikon on how the Octoechos must be used with the Menaion.

units.english_text: 6. The Heirmologion [Chant-Book] (in Greek: *Heirmologion* [Ἑιρμολόγιον], from the word: *heirmon* [εἱρμὸν] = *melodia vel series* [melody or chain/series]). It is so called because it containeth in musical notes various church chants, especially from the Octoechos, but besides this also taken from the Menaion, from the Triodion, and from other books, which in church must be sung and not read, and according to which many other hymns are also sung. It is likewise for the most part an abridged Octoechos, but since it also hath hymns taken from other books which are set here to musical notes, therefore in this sense it is an excerpt from all the principal books. Most particularly it containeth in itself: The Heirmologisation of the Octoechos, which is divided according to the 8 tones, that is, melodies. In each tone there is set in notes: (α) How the stichera at “Lord, I have cried” are to be sung with the dogmatica and with the doxastica [slavy]; (β) Sunday Troparia with sessional hymns and graduals [stepenny]; (γ) Heirmoi of the canon with exaposteilaria; (δ) Then model hymns [prosomoia] and Bulgarian chants, etc. — With each tone there are also stichera of the great feasts which at Great Vespers are sung in place of Sunday dogmatica. After the eighth tone there are various hymns and chants taken from other books, such as: the Polyeleos [*Mnohomylostyven*], Exaltations [Velichaniya], the hymn “We who the Cherubim” [Cherubic Hymn], “All of creation rejoiceth in thee,” chants of the Liturgy of the Presanctified, and the thanksgiving hymn of St. Ambrose: “We praise Thee, O God” [*Te Deum*].

units.english_text: 7. The Monthly Books [Menaia] (in Greek: *Menaia biblia* [Μηναῖα βιβλία] = *libri mensuales*, from the word: *men* [μὴν] = month). They consist of 12 books for the 12 months, in which are arranged the services for immovable feasts. Every Saint concerning whose life church history knoweth anything, and all church events whose memory holy Church celebrateth, have their proper services and their morning canons, so that their number reacheth up to 800.[^37] Each book containeth in itself: (α) If there be a lesser or non-festal Saint: evening stichera, further the morning canon, and Troparia of lesser Saints; (β) If there be a middle Saint, then at Vespers it hath stichera on 6, the rest as for lesser Saints; (γ) If there be a great Saint, then it containeth Great Vespers with stichera and with readings, sometimes also a Litiya — and the entire divine service is taken from the Menaion; (δ) It containeth in itself the divine service of Marian Feasts; (ε) Of Feasts of the Lord, only the divine service of immovable feasts is found here. At the end of each single book there are: (α) Sunday Theotokia of the Resurrection in 8 tones sung at “Lord, I have cried” and at the aposticha; (β) Theotokia of the 8 tones which on weekdays, when there is a “Glory” to the Saint in the Menaion, are taken at “Now and ever”; (γ) Sunday dismissal Theotokia in 8 tones sung after the Sunday Troparia at “Now and ever”; (δ) Dismissal Theotokia for weekdays in 8 tones sung after the Troparia at Vespers, and at Matins at “The Lord is God” and at the conclusion.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: ков которыя на вел вечерни место недельных догматов
units.slavonic_text: ковъ, которыя на вел. Вечерни мѣсто недѣльныхъ догматовъ спѣваются. По осьмомъ гласѣ сѫть различныя пѣсни и пѣнія взятыя изъ дрѹгихъ книгъ, такъ: многомилостивенъ (полѵелей), величанія, пѣснь „Иже Херѹвимы“, „О тебѣ радѹется“, пѣсни Слѹжб. Преждеосвященныхъ и пѣснь благодарственная св. Амвросія „Тебе Бога хвалимъ“.
units.english_text: 8. The Anthologion (in Greek: *Anthologion* [᾿Ανθολόγιον], from the word: *anthos* [ἄνθος] = *flos*, flower; or: *Tryphologion* [Τρυφολόγιον], from the word: *tryphe* [τρύφη] = *deliciae* [delights]). This book is nothing other than an abridged Menaion, which is also called the “Festal Menaion,” and that because it containeth in itself all those services of immovable feasts of the Lord, Marian feasts, and great Saints which are found also in the Menaion. Besides this, the Anthologion containeth in itself at the end of the second volume also the common services for middle and lesser Saints according to various ranks [choirs], and therefore this part is called: The General Menaion, that is, the *Obshchina*. This book containeth in itself: (a) If there be a Feast of the Lord: (α) Stichera of Small Vespers; (β) Stichera of Great Vespers with readings; (γ) Stichera at the Litiya with stichera at the aposticha; (δ) Three morning sessional hymns; (ε) The sticheron sung after Psalm 50; (ϑ) The Magnification refrain in place of “My soul doth magnify the Lord”; (η) An exaposteilarion; (ι) Stichera at the Praises; (κ) Antiphons at the Liturgy; (λ) Stichera of the Afterfeast sung at Vespers; (b) If there be a Marian Feast, then everything is found just as at Feasts of the Lord, except at Matins, for here after the 8th ode there is no magnification refrain; if there be a refrain, it is found in the Psalter; (c) If there be a great Saint, then it is one case if there be a Litiya, and another if there be no Litiya. If there be a Litiya, then it containeth in itself: (α) Small Vespers with 4 stichera at “Lord, I have cried” and with stichera at the aposticha; (β) Great Vespers with stichera at “Lord, I have cried” and readings, and with stichera at the Litiya and with stichera at the aposticha; Matins with canons, which concludeth in regular order. If there be no Litiya, then it containeth in itself: (α) Stichera of Great Vespers with readings, and with stichera at the aposticha; (β) Three morning sessional hymns; (γ) The sticheron sung after Psalm 50; (δ) Three canons: the first to the Theotokos, and the second and third to the Saint; (ε) Stichera at the Praises; (d) Finally, if there be a middle or lesser Saint, the service is taken from the General Menaion [*Obshchina*]. In the General Menaion the Saint hath: (α) Three stichera at Vespers; “Glory and now”: a Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion; (β) At Matins he hath a canon, sometimes also an exaposteilarion.

units.slavonic_incipit: праздниковъ Господскихъ Богородичныхъ и великихъ Святыхъ,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: праздников господских богородичных и великих святых которыя и
units.slavonic_text: праздниковъ Господскихъ Богородичныхъ и великихъ Святыхъ, которыя и въ Минеи находятся. Кромѣ сего Цвѣтословъ содержитъ въ себѣ на концѣ второй книги и общія Отправы для средныхъ и меньшихъ Святыхъ по разнымъ ликамъ и прото сія часть называется: Общею Минеею, т. е. Общиною. Сія книга содержитъ въ себѣ: a) Если есть праздникъ Господскій: α) Стихиры малой Вечерни. β) Стихиры великой Вечерни съ чтеніями. γ) Стихиры на Литіи съ стихирами на стиховнѣхъ. δ) Три сѣдалны оутренныи. ε) Стихирѹ поемѹю по 50-омъ Чалмѣ. ϑ) Припѣвкъ вмѣсто „Величитъ дѹша моя“. η) Свѣтиленъ. ι) Стихиры на „Хвалите“-хъ. κ) Антифоны на Литѹргіи. λ) Стихиры Попразденства на Вечерни поемыя. b) Если же есть праздникъ Богородичный, то все такъ находится, какъ въ праздникахъ Господскихъ, изявше на Оутрени, ибо здѣсь по 8-ой пѣсни нѣтъ припѣква; если же есть припѣвъ, то въ Чалтырѣ находится. c) Если же есть великій Святый, тогда иный слѹчай, если есть Литіа, и опять иный, если нѣтъ Литіи. Если есть Литіа, тогда въ себѣ содержитъ: α) Малѹю Вечерню съ 4-ми стихирами на „Господи воззвахъ“ и съ стихирами на стиховнѣхъ. β) Великѹю Вечерню съ стихирами на „Господи воззвахъ“ и чтеніями и съ стихирами на Литіи и съ стихирами на стиховнѣхъ; Оутреню съ канонами, которая порядочно кончится. Если же нѣтъ Литіи, тогда въ себѣ содержитъ: α) Стихиры великой Вечерни съ чтеніями, и съ стихирами на стиховнѣхъ. β) Три сѣдалны оутренныи. γ) Стихирѹ по 50-омъ Чалмѣ поемѹю. δ) Три каноны: первый Богородицѣ, а вторый и третій Святомѹ. ε) Стихиры на „Хвалите“-хъ. d) На конецъ, если есть средній или малый Святый, то отправа берется изъ Общины. Въ Общинѣ Святый имѣетъ: α) Три стихиры на Вечерни. Слава и Нынѣ: Богородиченъ или Крестобогородиченъ. β) На Оутрени имѣетъ канонъ, нѣкогда и свѣтиленъ.
units.english_text: 10. The Apostol (in Greek: *Apostolos* [᾿Απόστολος] or *Apostolikon biblion* [᾿Αпоστολικὸν βιβλίον]). It containeth in itself: (α) The Acts of the Apostles, writ- ten by the Holy Evangelist Luke; (β) The General [Catholic] Epistles of the Holy Apostles: James, Peter, John, and Jude; (γ) The Epistles of the Holy Apostle Paul to various churches or persons, thus: to the Romans, 2 to the Corinthians, to the Galatians, to the Ephesians, to the Philippians, to the Colossians, 2 to the Thessalonians, 2 to Timothy, to Titus, to Philemon, and to the Hebrews. — The Apostol with respect to ecclesiastical use is divided into pericopes [*pericopae* / *zachala*], of which there are 339. The numbering by pericopes beginneth from the first chapter of the Acts of the Apostles and proceedeth through all the apostolic epistles in the cited order, even unto the end of the Epistle to the Hebrews. In the margin it is indicated when at the beginning of the reading one must begin: “In those days,” when: “Brethren,” when: “Child Titus,” or: “Child Timothy!” — At the end of the book there is found a direction when and how the appointed portions from the epistles are to be read.[^38]

units.english_text: 11. The Gospel (in Greek: *Evangelion* [Εὐαγγέλιον], from the words: *eu* and *angelia* [εὖ et ἀγγελία] = *laetus nuntius* [glad tidings]). It containeth in itself the life and teaching of Jesus Christ set forth by the four Evangelists. The Gospels are divided into chapters and verses, but this division is scholastic; for ecclesiastical use there is the division into pericopes [*zachala*]; — and thus the Gospel of St. Matthew is divided into 115, of St. Mark into 71, of St. Luke into 114, and of St. John into 67 pericopes. At the end the Gospels have an index [rubric] showing what Gospel ought to be read and when, and that firstly according to movable feasts, beginning from the Sunday of Pascha, then according to immovable feasts, beginning from September 1, and lastly according to various occasions and needs. In order that this pericope might be more easily found, there is indicated in the text at the bottom, usually in red letters, that same designation, and therewith are added also the words with which the respective pericope is to begin, which are: “The Lord said,” “The Lord said to His disciples,” “The Lord said to the Jews that came unto Him,” or “The Lord spoke this parable,” or “At that time.” — After these words a red star is printed, directing to the first word of the pericope which must be read, and beside that word there is likewise a star.

The Sluzhebnik (in Greek: *Leitourgikon* [Λειτουργικόν], from the word: *leitourgein* [λειτουργεῖν] = *munus publicum obire* [to perform a public duty/office], which word is composed of *leiton* and *ergon* [λεῖτον et ἔργον] = *publicum* et *munus* [public and duty]). It containeth in itself: (α) All things necessary for the Holy Liturgy, namely: Antiphons, Troparia, Prokeimena, Epistles, and Gospels, Exaltations [Velichaniya],[^39] Communion Hymns, and dismissals of Sundays, feasts, and plain movable days, and that: beginning from the Sunday of Pascha unto the Sunday of All Saints, furthermore from the Sunday of All Saints unto the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee, and from thence unto Great Saturday; (β) The Order of the Divine Liturgies: of St. John Chrysostom, of St. Basil the Great, and of St. Gregory the Dialogist, that is, of the Presanctified; (γ) Services of the entire year for immovable feasts, and that: Feasts of the Lord, Marian Feasts, and proper to Saints; (δ) General services for other Saints having no proper services in the Menologion; (ε) Services of various intentions; (ϛ) The Order of Vespers with Litiya, the Order of the Midnight Office, both Sunday and daily, and the Order of Matins; (η) Sunday Troparia, Kontakia, and Theotokia of the eight tones; (ϑ) Daily and general Troparia to the Saints; (ι) The prayer over kolyvo (offering), and “We praise Thee, O God.”

units.english_text: 13. The Trebnik [Euchologion] (in Greek: *Euchologion* [Εὐχολόγιον], from the word: *euche* [εὐχὴ] = *praecatio* [prayer]). It is called in the Old Slavonic language “Trebnik” from its principal content, that is, from the Holy Mysteries [Sacraments], which are indispensably necessary [*potrebny*] to men, or also because daily necessities can be satisfied through these services. It containeth in itself: (α) The rites of the seven Holy Mysteries. It must be noted that the priest will find also in the Trebnik those rules which he must observe during the administration of the Holy Mysteries; (β) Services of every kind of ecclesiastical Consecrations and Blessings, such as: the Order of Burials, the Order of Parastas, the Order of the Consecration and Blessing of water, church, cemetery, bells, vestments, vessels, objects, fruits, herbs, etc.; (γ) Various prayers, such as: that concluded at the beginning of the Holy Forty Days, for the blessing of palms, of meats, over the sick, in time of fair weather and drought, etc.; (δ) The Order of the installation of a newly appointed pastor, further the rubric on the Divine Liturgy celebrated by a priest for the first time, and then a second time after 50 years; (ε) At the end there is also the profession of faith which a priest, pastor, professor of theology, canon, and bishop must profess.

units.english_text: 15. The Typikon (in Greek: *Typikon* [Τυπικὸν], from the word: *typos* [τύπος] = *forma*, *regula* [form, rule]) is the rubrical order, or guide, for how the divine services of the entire year are to be celebrated from all the above-mentioned books. The Typikon which is used among us[^40] was published for the Eparchy of Przemyśl; it is divided into the following parts: (α) On the ecclesiastical rule in general; (β) On the order of sacred ministrations, that is, how Small and Great Vespers, Compline, the Midnight Office, Matins, the Hours, the Typika [*Obidnytsia*], and the Liturgy are celebrated in general; (γ) Special directions for the most notable immovable feasts in the order of the Menologion, beginning from September 1; (δ) Special directions for movable feasts, Sundays, and weekdays from the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee even unto the Sunday of All Saints; (ε) Directions on the Polyeleos, the ordinary Katavasia, the hymn “My soul doth magnify the Lord,” on the Typika [*Izobrazitelni*] and Antiphons, and on dismissals with supplementary notes; (ϛ) Finally, it containeth six pillars [stólpy] with the incipits of the Gospel pillars taken from the Indiction, and a brief Paschalion direction. The Typikon was compiled on the foundation of the church books, to which it frequently referreth, and in which explanation must be sought if anything in the Typikon should be stated incompletely or not entirely clearly.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 15 типик по гречески от слова
units.slavonic_text: 15. Типикъ, (по гречески: „Τύπικον“ отъ слова: τύπος == forma, regula) есть оуставъ, либо рѹководство, какъ имѣютъ богослѹженія цѣлаго года изъ всѣхъ вышепомянѹтыхъ книгъ отправлятися. Типикъ, который оу насъ оупотребляется*) есть для епархіи Перемышльской выданъ; раздѣляется на слѣдѹющія части: α) О правилѣ церковномъ вообще. β) О оуставѣ священнослѹженій, т. е. какъ совершается Вечерня малая и великая, Повечеріе, Полѹнощница, Оутреня, Часы и Обѣдница и Литѹргія вообще. γ) Оуказаніе особенное, изряднѣйшимъ праздникамъ недвижимымъ по рядѹ мѣсяцослова, заченше отъ 1-го Сент. δ) Оуказаніе особенное по праздникамъ движимымъ, недѣлямъ и днямъ седмичнымъ отъ Нед. о Мытари и Фарисеи, даже до Недѣли всѣхъ Святыхъ. ε) Оуказы о полѵелеи, катавасіи рядовой, пѣсни „Величитъ“, о изобразительныхъ и антифонахъ и объ отпѹстахъ съ дополнительными примѣчаніями. ϛ) На конецъ содержитъ шесть столповъ съ началами столповъ Евангелійныхъ вынятыми изъ Индиктіона, и короткій оуказъ Пасхаліи. Типикъ составленъ на основѣ книгъ церковныхъ, на которыя часто отзывается, и въ которыхъ нѹждно искати поясненіа, если бы въ Типикѣ нѣчто не полно, либо не совсѣмъ ясно было сказанно.
units.english_text: (α) The Molitvoslov, or better said, the “Priestly Horologion,” for it containeth in itself everything that the Horologion containeth, but besides this priestly needs are also satisfied here; (β) The Izbornik of needful ecclesiastical rites and services taken from the Horologion, Leitourgikon, Octoechos, Menaion, and Triodion; (γ) The “Sunday Octoechos,” which containeth in itself only the Sunday service; (δ) The “Strastnik” [Passion Book], that is, the book containing the Gospels that are read in Passion Week; (ε) The “Hlasopesnets,” containing in itself the most frequently used chants of the Heirmologion and other church hymns; (ϛ) The “Bohohlasnyk” (in Greek: *hymnologion* [ὑμνολόγιον]), containing in itself church hymns in musical notes;[^41] (η) The “Akathistnik,” which containeth in itself 20 Akathists.

units.english_text: Public books are divided in accordance with church rites into 3 parts, and that into: (α) Choral, (β) Liturgical, and (γ) Euchological books (*libri chorales, liturgici et euchologici*).[^42] Choral books contain in themselves pre-liturgical services, and these are: the Horologion, Psalter, Triodion, Pentecostarion, Octoechos, Menaia (or the Anthologion with the General Menaion), and the Synaxarion. Liturgical books contain the services of the Holy Liturgies, and these are: the Leitourgikon, Apostol, and Gospel. Lastly, euchological books contain in themselves the rites of the Holy Mysteries and other ecclesiastical Consecrations and Blessings; to these belongeth: the Trebnik.

units.english_text: 1. The Psalter is so divided in the services that in each week the entire Psalter is to be read through once, and in the Great Fast in each week (with the exception of Passion Week) twice; — in Passion Week, however, when it is prescribed to read through all 4 Gospels, the entire Psalter is read in the first three days only once, namely all kathismata with the exception of the first three and the 17th, while the 18th kathisma at that time is read three times, namely each day at Vespers. On other days, just as also in Bright Week, the Psalter is omitted.

units.slavonic_text: Книги пѹбличныѧ раздѣляются соотвѣтно обрядамъ церковнымъ на 3 части, и то на книги: α) хоралныя, β) литѹргичныѧ и γ) евхологичныѧ (libri chorales, liturgici et euchologici.*) Хоралныя книги въ себѣ содержатъ отправы предлитѹргичныѧ, и тѣ сѫть: Часословъ, Чалтырь, Тріодь, Пентекостарь, Октоихъ, Минеи (или Трифолой съ Общиною) и Синаксарь. Литѹргичныѧ же книги отправы св. Литѹргій и тѣ сѫть: Литѹргиконъ, Апостолъ и Евангеліе. На послѣдъ книги евхологичныѧ въ себѣ содержатъ обряды св. Таинъ и прочіихъ Освященій и Благословеній церковныхъ, къ симъ принадлежитъ: Требникъ.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: святых до недели о мытари и фарисеи октоих
units.slavonic_text: Святыхъ до Недѣли о Мытари и Фарисеи Октоихъ съ Минеею, въ постѣ же Тріодь съ Октоихомъ и съ Минеею, въ часъ Пятдесятницы же Тріодь Цвѣтная съ Минеею.
units.english_text: 4. The Lenten Triodion is joined with the Octoechos in such wise that: (α) On the days of Cheesefare Week there are taken from the Octoechos at Vespers the stichera at “Lord, I have cried,” and at Matins the sessional hymns after the first stichology, exaposteilaria, and those odes of the canon which are not in the Triodion; (β) On the Sundays of the Great Fast, besides the Triodion, the Octoechos is also taken, with the exception of Palm Sunday; (γ) On the weekdays of the Forty Days there are taken from the Octoechos at Matins the sessional hymns after the 1st stichology, but the canon of the Octoechos is superseded by the Triodion [three odes] and this canon on weekdays is entirely omitted. In a word, concerning the Octoechos we can say this: that the chanting of the Octoechos, regarding weekdays, beginneth on Monday after the Sunday of All Saints and in regular order concludeth on Friday before Meatfare Saturday, and exceptionally endeth on Friday before Lazarus Saturday; regarding Sundays, however, it beginneth on the second Sunday after the Descent of the Holy Spirit and continueth unto the 5th Sunday of the Great Fast inclusively. Because parts of the Octoechos are printed at the end of the Menaion, or in the Menaion itself, we can say that in the Great Fast the Octoechos is taken only on Sundays, and on weekdays is omitted. But besides this, the Lenten Triodion is combined also with the Menaion, namely: on all weekdays of the Forty Days there are taken, besides the Triodion, at Vespers from the Menaion 3 or 4 stichera at “Lord, I have cried,” and at Matins the canon of the occurring Saint, which, with slight exceptions indicated in the Triodion, is sung in its entirety.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 4 триод постная соединяется с октоихом так что
units.slavonic_text: 4. Тріодь Постная соединяется съ Октоихомъ такъ, что: α) Въ дни сырной седмицѣ берѹтся изъ Октоиха на Вечерни стихиры на Господи воззвахъ, а на Оутрени сидалны по первомъ стихословіи, свѣтилны и тіи пѣсни канона, которыхъ въ Тріоди не есть. β) Въ Недѣли великаго Поста кромѣ Тріоди берется и Октоихъ, съ взятіемъ Недѣли Цвѣтоносной. γ) Въ седмичны же дни Четыредесятницы берется изъ Октоиха на Оутрени сидалны по 1-омъ стихословіи, канонъ же Октоиха Трипѣснецемъ застѹпается и сей канонъ въ седмичныи дни цѣлкомъ оставляется. Словомъ касательно Октоиха можемъ то сказати, что: пѣніе Октоиха, касательно седмичныхъ дней, зачинается въ Понедѣлокъ по Недѣли всѣхъ Святыхъ и порядочно кончится въ Пятокъ передъ Сѹбботѹ мясопѹстнѹю, чрезвычайно же окончится въ Пятокъ передъ Сѹбботѹ Лазаревѹ; касательно же недѣль зачинается въ вторѹю Недѣлю по Сошествіи св. Дѹха и продолжается до 5-ой Недѣли Великаго Поста включно. Понеже части Октоиха при концѣ Минеи, либо въ самой Минеи сѫть напечатанны: то можемъ сказати, что въ В. Постѣ Октоихъ токмо по Недѣлямъ берется, а въ седмичніи дни оставляется. Но кромѣ сего Тріодь постная соединяется такожь и съ Минеею, именно: въ всѣ дни седмичныѧ Четыредесятницы берется кромѣ Тріоди на Вечерни изъ Минеи 3 либо 4 стихиры на Господи воззвахъ, а на Оутрени канонъ слѹчившагося Святаго, который съ малыми взятіями въ Тріоди оуказанными цѣлый спивается.
units.english_text: 5. The Octoechos is omitted: (α) From Lazarus Saturday even unto the Sunday of All Saints inclusively, with the exception of certain parts which are taken from the Octoechos and transferred to the Flower Triodion and printed here; (β) From December 20 unto January 14, with the exception of a single Sunday; (γ) On great Feasts of the Lord, on whatever day they fall, even on a Sunday; (δ) On great Marian Feasts, if they fall on a weekday; (if a Marian Feast falleth on a Sunday, the Sunday service is taken from the Octoechos, and the feast from the Menaion); (ε) Likewise also during Forefeasts and at the Apodoses (excepting Sundays) of great feasts; (ϛ) And on the feasts of Great Saints (excepting Sundays) the Octoechos is omitted.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 5 октоих оставляется от субб лаз аж
units.slavonic_text: 5 Октоихъ оставляется: α) Отъ Сѹбб. Лаз. ажъ до Нед. всѣхъ Святыхъ включно съ взятіемъ нѣкоторыхъ частей, которыя изъ Октоиха сѫть взяты и въ Тріодь Цвѣтнѹю сѫть преложенны и тѹй выпечатанны. β) Отъ 20. Дек. до 14. Янв. изявше одной Недѣли. γ) Въ великіи праздники Господскіи, въ якій нибѹдь день они припадѹтъ, хотя и въ Недѣлю. δ) Въ великіи праздники Богородичніи, если они въ день седмичный припадаютъ; (если же праздникъ Богородичный припадаетъ въ Недѣлю, то берется слѹжба Недѣли изъ Октоиха, а изъ Минеи праздникъ.) ε Такожде и въ предпразденства и въ предпразденства и въ отданіа (изявше Недѣли) великихъ праздниковъ. ϛ) И въ праздники великихъ Святыхъ (изявше Недѣли) Октоихъ оставляется.
units.english_text: 6. The Menaion is omitted: (α) On all Sundays of the Lenten Triodion, beginning from the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee unto Palm Sunday inclusively; (β) On Wednesday and Friday of the 3rd week and on Thursday of the 5th week of the Great Fast; (γ) On Saturdays, namely Meatfare, Cheesefare, of the 1st and 5th weeks, and on Lazarus Saturday; (δ) On all days of Passion Week.

units.english_text: Note: But if on those days there should occur a Great Saint, or the Patron Saint of the church, or the Feast of the Meeting and the Annunciation, their service is taken even on the cited days. Nevertheless, here too there are limitations, thus: the service of the “40 Martyrs” is not taken if those Saints occur on Thursday or Saturday of the fifth week; the service of St. John the Forerunner is not taken on Meatfare Saturday if it falleth on February 24; only the service of the Meeting is always taken on its proper day, and the service of the Annunciation is celebrated even in Passion Week; the service of a Great or Patron Saint in Passion Week is taken in the first days, but in the latter days is transferred to Bright Week on Monday.

units.slavonic_text: включно. β) Въ Середѹ и Пятокъ 3-ой седмицы и въ Четверъ 5-ой седмицы Вел. Поста. γ) Въ Сѹбботы, такъ въ мясопѹстнѹю, сыропѹстнѹю, 1-ой и 5-ой седмицы и въ Сѹбб. Лазаревѹ. δ) Въ всѣ дни страстной седмицы.
units.english_text: 7. The Flower Triodion is taken together with the Menaion from Thomas Sunday even unto the Sunday of All Saints, and that usually so that at Vespers there are taken at “Lord, I have cried” 3 stichera from the Menaion, and the canon on 4. Nevertheless, during this time the Menaion is omitted: (α) On all days of Bright Week; (β) On all Sundays of Pentecost; (γ) On the day of Mid-Pentecost and its Apodosis; (δ) On the day of the Apodosis of Pascha; (ε) On the day of Ascension and its Apodosis; (ϛ) On the Saturday before Pentecost; (η) On the feast of the Descent of the Holy Spirit on Sunday and on Monday; (ϑ) On the Sunday of All Saints. Nevertheless, although the services of middle Saints are transferred on these days, those of Great Saints, and especially of Patron Saints of the church, are celebrated on their proper days, even though they should occur on the cited days.

units.slavonic_incipit: Примѣчаніе: Но если бы въ тіи
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: примечание но если бы в тии дни случился
units.slavonic_text: Примѣчаніе: Но если бы въ тіи дни слѹчился великій Святый, альбо Святый храмовый, альбо праздникъ Стрѣтеніа и Благовѣщеніа, то ихъ слѹжба и въ наведенніи дни берется. Однакожь и тѹй сѫть ограниченія, такъ: слѹжба „40 мѹчениковъ“ не берется, если тіи Святіи слѹчатся въ Четверъ или Сѹбботѹ пятой седмицы; слѹжба св. Іоанна Предт. не берется въ Сѹбботѹ мясопѹстнѹю, если тая на 24. Февр. припадаетъ, только слѹжба Стрѣтеніа всегда берется въ свой день, и слѹжба Благовѣщеніа отправляется и въ страстнѹю седмицѹ, слѹжба же великаго или храмоваго святаго въ страстной седмицѣ въ первые дни берется, но въ послѣдные дни прелагается въ свѣтлѹю седмицѹ на Понедѣлникъ.
units.english_text: Note: The services of Lesser and Middle Saints which are omitted from Lazarus Saturday unto Thomas Sunday are taken anticipatively [*anticipative*] from Monday of the 2nd week of the Great Fast at Compline.

provenance.verbatim_source: Note: The services of Lesser and Middle Saints which are omitted from Lazarus Saturday unto Thomas Sunday are taken anticipatively [*anticipative*] from Monday of the 2nd week of the Great Fast at Compline.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 7 триод цветная берется разом с минеею от
units.slavonic_text: 7. Тріодь цвѣтная берется разомъ съ Минеею отъ Нед. Ѳом. ажъ до Нед. Всѣхъ Святыхъ, и то такъ обычайно, что на Вечерни берѹтся на Господи воззвахъ 3 стихиры изъ Минеи, а канонъ на 4. Однакожь въ семъ часѣ Минеа оставляется: α) въ всѣ дни свѣтлой седмицы; β) въ всѣ недѣли Пятдесятницы; γ) въ день преполовенія и его отданіа; δ) въ день отданіа Пасхи; ε) въ день Вознесеніа и его отданіа; ϛ) въ Сѹбботѹ предъ Пятдесятницею; η) въ праздникъ Сош. св. Дѹха въ Недѣлю и въ Понедѣлокъ; ϑ) въ Нед. всѣхъ Святыхъ. Однакожь, хотя слѹжбы средныхъ святыхъ въ сіи дни прелагаются, но великихъ Святыхъ, особенно же храмовыхъ Святыхъ отправляются въ ихъ дни, хотяй бы слѹчилися и наведенныи дни.
units.english_text: 8. The singing of the eight tones of the Octoechos in the course of 8 weeks is called a “pillar” [*stolp*]. Of pillars throughout one year there are 6; they begin at an appointed time: the 1st pillar beginneth on the 1st Sunday of the Fast of the Apostles [Peter and Paul]; the 2nd on the days after the Prophet Elijah; the 3rd after the Exaltation of the Precious Cross; the 4th during the Fast of the Nativity of the Lord; the 5th after Theophany; and the 6th during the Holy Great Fast. — If anyone wisheth to know on which day of each year each single pillar falleth: let him first look up from the Indiction the Key-letter [*klyuch hranychnyi*], that is, the boundary letter, and thereafter let him look under this letter in the Paschalion, and there it is accurately stated on what day each pillar beginneth.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: в и ом столетии христиане из
units.slavonic_text: Въ I., II. и III-омъ столѣтіи Христіане изъ книгъ церковныхъ вѣроятно не имѣли лишь св. Писаніе Ветх. и Новаго Завѣта и Псалтырь.
units.english_text: In the 6th century lived St. Sabbas († 532), Archimandrite of the “Great Lavra” on the torrent Cedron near Jerusalem, who composed a multitude of chants and canticles and one church order, which is now known under the name of the “Typikon of St. Sabbas.” — Besides this, he is also held to be the first compiler of the Menaion. He systematically compiled the Menaion according to oral tradition, which he received from his teachers St. Chariton (who lived in the time of Constantine), St. Euthymius († 473), and St. Theoctistus († 467),[^44] and prescribed it with obligation for his monks.

He composed, among others, the canon for the Descent of the Holy Spirit.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: глава
units.slavonic_text: ГЛАВА III.
units.english_text: By technical terms we call those names by which we designate the psalms and poems, readings, liturgical actions and melodies, hymns, chants and canticles, parts and entire services used in our rite. — Those designations were received by the respective parts of our rite either according to text, or melody, or composition, or usage, or purpose, or according to their meaning. Thus the kontakion received this name from the text, for it is a short poem (*kontakion* [κοντάκιον] == *breviculum*); psalms are called antiphons from their melody; the polyeleos received this name from its composition, for therein the word *eleos* [ἔлеος] == *mercy* is found many times; the refrain [*pripiv*] is so called from its usage, for it is chanted before a troparion; the prokimenon is so named from its purpose, for by it the faithful are reminded of the reading of Holy Scripture; while the parastas is so called according to its meaning (*parastasis* [παράστασις] == *intercessio*), for by it we intercede for the departed.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 1 чин по гречески так оупотребляется как
units.slavonic_text: 1. „Чинъ“ (по гречески: „διάταξις“) такъ оупотребляется, какъ рядъ нѣкаго дѣйствія божественнаго (ordo seu dispositio officii divini.) 2. „Служба“ (по гречески: „᾿Ακολουθία“ == ipsum officium) же не есть ино, какъ самое дѣйствіе въ рядѣ низложенное (ipsum officium ordinatum denotat.) 3. „Псалмы“ суть гимны изъ В. Завѣта взаты и называются псалмами (по гречески: „ψάλμος“) отъ слова: „ψάλλειν“, ибо Юдеи тѣ поюще ихъ съ музикою сопровождали. Изъ псалмовъ знаменитнѣйшіи суть: α) Псаломъ 103-ый („Благослови душе моя“), который называется псалмомъ предначинательнымъ, (по гречески: „προοιμιακὸς“ == prooimialis), ибо нимъ зачинается правило церковное. β) Псаломъ 140-ый („Господи воззвахъ“), называется псалмомъ свѣтильничнымъ, (по гречески: „ὁ ἐπιλύχνιος“ == lucernarius), и то прото, ибо на вечерней жертвѣ давно той псаломъ стихословили при той свички, которую діаконъ вынесъ и поставилъ предъ царскими вратами, либо прото, что на вечерни передъ свѣтомъ жертвы вечерней стихословится. γ) Псалмы: 3., 37., 62., 87., 102. и 142. называются „Шестопсалміе“-мъ, (по гречески: „ἑξάψαλμος“ отъ словъ: „ἕξ“ et „ψάλμος“.) δ) Псаломъ 118-ый („Блаженны непорочніи“), называется псалмомъ непорочнымъ, (по гречески: „ὁ ἄμωμος“) и то прото, ибо въ немъ описуетъ блаженство непорочнаго человѣка. ε) Псаломъ 135-ый („Исповѣдайтеся Господеви“), называется псалмомъ многомилостивнымъ, (по гречески: „ὁ πολυέλεος“.) Названіе сіе происходитъ отъ туда, что въ тѣхъ стихахъ псалма часто повторяется слово „милость“, по гречески: „ἔλεος“. ζ) Псалмы 119—133-ый называются псалмами степенными, (по гречески: „ἀναβαθμοί“ == psalmi graduales), и то прото, что въ Псалтырѣ передъ псалмомъ 118-ымъ найдемъ надпись: „Пѣснь степеней“. units.english_text: 3. **Psalms** are hymns taken from the Old Testament and are called psalms (in Greek: *psalmos* [ψάλμος]) from the word *psallein* [ψάλλειν], for the Hebrews, when singing them, accompanied them with music. Of the psalms the most renowned are: (α) Psalm 103 (“Bless the Lord, O my soul”), which is called the introductory psalm (in Greek: *prooimiakos* [προοιμιακὸς] == *prooimialis*), for with it the church rule beginneth; (β) Psalm 140 (“Lord, I have cried”), called the lucernarium psalm (in Greek: *ho epilychnios* [ὁ ἐπιλύχνιος] == *lucernarius*), and that because at the evening sacrifice of old that psalm was stichologized by the light of that candle which the deacon brought out and placed before the royal doors, or because at Vespers it is stichologized before the lighting of the evening sacrifice; (γ) Psalms 3, 37, 62, 87, 102, and 142 are called the “Six Psalms” [Hexapsalmos] (in Greek: *hexapsalmos* [ἑξάψαλμος], from the words *hex* [ἕξ] and *psalmos* [ψάλμος]); (δ) Psalm 118 (“Blessed are the undefiled”), called the blameless psalm (in Greek: *ho amomos* [ὁ ἄμωμος]), and that because therein is described the blessedness of the blameless man; (ε) Psalm 135 (“O give thanks unto the Lord”), called the polyeleos psalm (in Greek: *ho polyeleos* [ὁ πολυέλεος]), and this name deriveth from the fact that in those verses of the psalm the word “mercy” is frequently repeated (in Greek: *eleos* [ἔλεος]); (ϛ) Psalms 119–133 are called gradual psalms (in Greek: *anabathmoi* [ἀναβαθμοί] == *psalmi graduales*), and that because in the Psalter before Psalm 119 we find the inscription: “A Song of Ascents.” The Holy Fathers say that the Hebrews sang those psalms when they returned from the Babylonian captivity; others say that they sang them during prayer pilgrimages to Jerusalem at the 3 great feasts. Besides this, some also say that those psalms were sung by the Levites at the Feast of Tabernacles while standing upon the 15 steps which were placed in the temple between the court of the men and the court of the women. Some also call those psalms also the psalms “unto the Lord” (*ta pros Kyrion* [τὰ πρὸς Κύριον]), and that because the first of them beginneth with this phrase: “unto the Lord”; (η) Psalms 148, 149, and 150 are called the laudatory psalms, or the psalms at the Praises [Lauds] (*hoi ainoi* [οἱ αἶνοι]), from the word *aineite* [αἰνεῖτε] == “praise ye,” which is repeated in the verses of these psalms; (ϑ) Psalm 102 (“Bless the Lord, O my soul”) and Psalm 145 (“Praise the Lord, O my soul”) are called the Typika psalms (*hoi ton typikon psalmoi* [οἱ τῶν τυπικῶν ψαλμοί]), for they proclaim the prefiguration (*typon* [τύπον] == *figuram*) of the Messiah coming into the world. They are stichologized at the Typika [Obyednytsia].

units.slavonic_incipit: ютъ тѣ псалмы еще и псалмами
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: ют те псалмы еще и псалмами к господу
units.slavonic_text: ютъ тѣ псалмы еще и псалмами „къ Господу“ („τὰ πρὸς Κύριον“) и то прото, ибо первый изъ нихъ зачинается: симъ словомъ: „къ Господу“. η) Псалмы 148., 149., 150. называются псалмами хвалительными, либо псалмами на Хвалите („οἱ αἶνοι“) отъ слова: „αἰνεῖτε“ == „хвалите“, которое въ стихахъ сихъ псалмовъ повторяется. ϑ) Псаломъ 102-ый („Благослови душе моя“) и Псаломъ 145-ый („Хвали душе моя“) называются псалмами изобразительными („οἱ τῶν τυπικῶν ψαλμοί“), ибо образъ („τύπον“ == figuram) въ міръ приходящаго Мессіи возвѣщаютъ. Они стихословятся на Обѣдницѣ.
units.english_text: 4. **Kathisma** (from the Greek word *kathizo* [κατίζω] == to sit) signifieth “a sitting.” The Psalter, as was said, containeth 20 kathismata. A kathisma was used in church either by reading or by chanting (*recitando vel cantando*). The reading of the Psalter was called “stichology” (*stichologia* [στηχολογία]), while the chanting was called “psalmody.” — When they only read (*aneu melous* [ἄνευ μέλους]) the Psalter, they divided the kathisma into 3 staseis (*staseis* [στασεῖς] == *stationes*), that is, at three places during the reading they rested. But when they sang (*meta melous* [μετὰ μέλους]), they divided the kathisma into 3 melodies. They read in such a manner that either one read with a single voice, or responsively [in two choirs]. But they chanted the kathisma in such a manner that: (α) either all sang together (*symphonia* [συμφωνία]), or (β) two choirs sang antiphonally (*antiphonia* [ἀνтиφωνία]), or (γ) two sang antiphonally and someone besides this was the leader (*hypophonia* [ὑποφωνία]),[^46] that is, the precentor (*hypoboleus* [ὑποβολεύς]) sang alone, and the others responded to him, either by repeating the final words of the psalm, or with another verse.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 4 кадизма ест наложенное оуставом церковным чтение псалтыря
units.slavonic_text: 4. „Кадизма“ есть наложенное оуставомъ церковнымъ чтеніе псалтыря, въ время котораго присутствующіи въ церкви могутъ сидѣти. Кадизма, отъ греческаго слова: „κατίζω“ == сидѣти, значитъ „сѣданіе.“ Псалтырь, якъ сказанно было, 20 кадизмъ имѣетъ. Кадизму оупотребляли въ церкви либо читающіе, либо спѣвающе (recitando vel cantando.) Чтеніе Псалтыря называлося „стихословіемъ“ (στηχολογία), пѣніе же „псалмодіею“. — Когда лишь читали (ἄνευ μέλους) Псалтырь, кадизму раздѣлили на 3 статіи („στασεῖς“ == stationes), то есть на трехъ мѣстахъ въ чтеніи отдыхли. Коли же спивали (μετά μέλους), кадизму раздѣлили на 3 мелодіи. Читали же такъ, что либо одинъ читалъ однимъ голосомъ, либо двоєкосно. Спѣвали же кадизму такъ, что α) либо всѣ вкупѣ спѣвали („συμφνία“), либо β) два клиросы противоположно спѣвали („ἀνтифонία“), либо γ) два противоположно спѣвали и нѣкто кромѣ сего былъ предводителемъ („ὑпофонία“),*) т. е. предводитель (ὑпоβολεύς) одинъ спѣвалъ, а прочіе ему отповидали, либо повторяючи послѣдныя слова псалма, либо инымъ стихомъ.
units.english_text: 5. **Antiphon** (in Greek: *antiphonon* [ἀντιφωνῶν]) signifieth nothing other than “responsive word” (*vox opposita, seu ejusdem vocis oppositio vel rectius ejusdem sententiae ad singulos versus psalmi repetitio*), that is: a corresponding and counter melody, or the repetition of a single divine thought throughout the verses of a psalm. Of the psalms, those which were chanted with a corresponding and antiphonal melody are called “antiphonal psalms,” or simply “Antiphons.” An antiphon in a nar- rower sense consisteth of 2 or 3 verses of a Psalm with “Glory” and “Now,” and of one refrain. Antiphonal psalms are the following: (α) Gradual psalms; (β) “Typika psalms” sung at the Typika [Obyednytsia]; (γ) “Liturgical psalms,” and those antiphons are either daily or festal. Daily antiphons are: Psalm 91 (“It is good to give praise unto the Lord”), thereafter Psalm 92 (“The Lord reigneth”), and Psalm 94 (“Come, let us rejoice in the Lord”). Of feasts, only the Feasts of Pascha, Ascension, Descent of the Holy Spirit, Transfiguration, Exaltation, Nativity of Jesus Christ, Theophany, and Meeting of our Lord in Jerusalem have proper antiphons. On Sunday and on other feasts it would be proper to sing the antiphonal psalms of the Typika, that is, Psalm 102 (“Bless the Lord, O my soul”), Psalm 145 (“Praise the Lord, O my soul”), and instead of the 3rd “antiphonal psalm” it would be proper to sing stichera composed on the individual verses of the evangelical Beatitudes spoken by Jesus Christ upon the mount in Matthew chapter 5, and therefore those are named “stichera on the Beatitudes.” But among us instead of those, Sunday antiphons are sung on Sundays.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: нейшем смысле состоит из 2 либо из 3
units.slavonic_text: нѣйшемъ смыслѣ состоитъ изъ 2, либо изъ 3 стиховъ Псалма съ „Слава“ и „Нынѣ“ и изъ однаго припѣва. Псалмы антифональніи суть сіи: α) псалмы степенніи, β) „псалмы изобразительніи“ на Обѣдницѣ поемыи, γ) „псалмы литургичныи“ и тѣ антифоны суть: либо дневніи, либо праздничніи. Дневніи антифоны суть: Псаломъ 91-ый („Благо есть исповѣдатися Господеви“), посемъ Псаломъ 92-ый („Господь воцарися“) и Псаломъ 94-ый („Прійдите возрадуемся Господеви“). Изъ праздниковъ лишь праздникъ Пасхи, Вознесеніа, Сошествіа св. Духа, Преображеніа, Воздвиженіа, Рождества І. Христа, Богоявленія и Срѣтенія Господа нашего въ Іерусалимъ имѣютъ антифоны. Оу Недѣлю и въ прочіи праздники потребно бы спѣвати псалмы антифональныи Обѣдницы т. е. Псаломъ 102-ый („Благослови душе моя“), Псаломъ 145-ый („Хвали душе моя“) и мѣсто 3-го „антифональнаго псалма“ потребно бы спѣвати стихиры, составленныя на единокіи стихи евангелскаго блаженства сказаннаго Іисусомъ Христомъ на горѣ оу Матѳея главѣ 5-ой, и прото тѣ названны „стихирами на Блаженнахъ“. Но оу насъ мѣсто тѣхъ по недѣлямъ поются антифоны воскресныи“.
units.english_text: 6. **Paroemia** (in Greek: *paroimia* [παροιμία] == *parabola, proverbium*). Paroemias are called readings from the Holy Scripture taken for the most part from the Old Testament and containing within themselves either prophecies concerning the event commemorated on that day, or explaining the event of the occurring feast, or containing praise thereof. But readings taken from the New Testament are called “Epistles” [*Apostles*] or “Gospels.” Paroemias are read: (α) At Great Vespers on Feasts of the Lord, of the Mother of God, and of Great Saints, usually 3; (β) In the Great Fast at Vespers, especially those combined with the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts,[^47] only 2; (γ) At Vespers combined with the Liturgy of St. Basil the Great, for example, on the Eves of the Nativity, of Theophany, and on Great Saturday, more; (δ) Besides this, they are also read at the Royal Hours, that is, on the Eve of the Nativity, of Theophany, and on Great Friday, but there at a single hour only one paroemia is taken.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 6 паримиа по гречески
units.slavonic_text: 6. Париміа (по гречески: παροιμία == parabola, proverbium.) Париміями называются чтеніа изъ св. Писанія по большей части изъ В. Завѣта взятыя и содержащія въ себѣ либо пророчества о событіи, которое въ той день воспоминается, либо объясняютъ событіе припадающаго праздника, либо содержатъ похвалу его. Изъ Н. Завѣта же взятыя чтенія называются „Апостолами“ или „Евангеліями“. Пареміи читаются: α) На вечерняхъ великихъ по праздникамъ Господскимъ, Богородичнымъ и Великимъ Святымъ обычайно 3. β) Въ великомъ постѣ же на Вечерняхъ, изряднѣе совокупшихъ съ Литургіею Преждеосвященныхъ Даровъ*) лишь 2. γ) На Вечерняхъ же совокупшихъ съ Литургіею св. Василія Вел., на пр. въ предпразденствахъ: Рождества, Богоявленія и Великой Субботы больше. δ) Кромѣ сего читаются еще они и на Часахъ Царскихъ, т. е. въ Навечеріи Рождества, Богоявленія и Вел. Пятка, но тѣй на одномъ часѣ лишь одна паремія берется.
units.english_text: 7. **The Canticles of Moses**. Concerning these canticles it is necessary to note that they are taken from various books of the Holy Scripture of the Old and New Testaments, namely: (α) Ode 1 is taken from Exodus 15:1–19; this canticle is that which, after passing through the Red Sea, Moses and the children of Israel sang thus: “Let us sing unto the Lord, for He hath been gloriously glorified”; (β) Ode 2 is taken from the Book of Deuteronomy, chapter 32, which Moses cried aloud at the end of his life, when he had led the people through the wilderness, tactics: “Give heed, O heaven, and I will speak”; (γ) Ode 3 is taken from 1 Kings [1 Samuel], chapter 2, and is the canticle of Hannah, mother of the Prophet Samuel, which she thus proclaimed: “My heart is established in the Lord”; (δ) Ode 4 is taken from the prophecy of Habakkuk, chapter 3, who having seen God coming forth from the shaded mountain, cried aloud thus: “Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid”; (ε) Ode 5 is taken from the book of the Prophet Isaiah, chapter 26, who having foretold the birth of Emmanuel from the Virgin, cried aloud thus: “Early in the morning my spirit seeketh Thee, O God”; (ϛ) Ode 6 is taken from the prophecy of Jonah, chapter 2:1–7, which he cried aloud when after his three-day stay in the belly of the whale he reached dry land, thus: “I cried in mine affliction unto the Lord God”; (η) Ode 7 is taken from the Book of Daniel, chapter 3, which the Three Youths cried aloud in the Babylonian furnace, saying thus: “Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers”; (ϑ) Ode 8 is likewise taken thence and containeth the thanksgiving canticle of those same youths delivered from the fiery furnace, which they cried aloud thus: “Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all forever”; (ι) Ode 9 is taken from the Gospel of St. Luke, chapter 1:68–79, which the Prophet Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, cried aloud when his son was born, thus: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel,” etc. At the beginning of this 9th Ode is found also the Canticle of the Theotokos in Luke, chapter 1:46, which she, bearing in her womb the Saviour, cried aloud thus: “My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.” — These Canticles of Moses are very important, for they are the foundation for the canons of the Sunday service. — Now they are read before the odes of the canon only in the Great Fast. Besides this, Ode 1 and Ode 8 are also sung on Great Saturday at Vespers between the 15 paroemias with beautiful hypophonia. Furthermore, it is necessary to note that when there was not yet a Sunday canon in the Church of Christ, these canticles were probably used.

units.slavonic_incipit: именно: α) Пѣснь I-ая взята есть
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: именно песн ая взята ест из исхода
units.slavonic_text: именно: α) Пѣснь I-ая взята есть изъ Исхода XV, 1—19, сія пѣснь есть та, которую по проходѣ черезъ море червеное воспѣлъ Мойсей и сынове Израилевы тако: „Поемъ Господеви, славно бо прославися“. β) Пѣснь II-ая взята изъ книги Второзаконной гл. XXXII., которую возопѣлъ Мойсей при концѣ жизни своей, когда перевелъ народъ черезъ пустыню, сяко: „Вонми небо и возглаголю“. γ) Пѣснь III-ая взята есть изъ кн. I. Царствъ гл. II. и есть пѣснь Анны, матери пророка Самуила, которую сякъ провозгласила: „Оутвердися сердце мое въ Господѣ“. δ) Пѣснь IV-ая взята изъ пророчества Аввакума гл. III., который видѣвше Бога грядущаго изъ горы преосѣненной, тако возопѣлъ: „Господи оуслышахъ слухъ Твой и оубояхся“. ε) Пѣснь V. взята изъ книги пророка Исаіи гл. XXVI., который когда предсказалъ рождество Еммануила отъ Дѣвы, тако возопѣлъ: „Отъ нощи оутренюетъ къ Тебѣ духъ мой Боже“. ζ) Пѣснь VI-ая взята изъ пророчества Іоны гл. II. 1—7., которую онъ тогда возопѣлъ, когда по тридневномъ событіи своемъ въ чревѣ кита достался на сушу, тако: „Возопіихъ въ скорби моей къ Господу Богу“. η) Пѣснь VII-ая взята есть изъ книги Даніила гл. III-ой, которую возопѣли три отроки въ пещи Вавилонской тако глаголюще: „Благословенъ еси Господи Боже Отецъ нашихъ“. ϑ) Пѣснь VIII-ая такожде взята есть отъ сяду и содержитъ въ себѣ благодарственную пѣснь тѣхъже отроковъ освободившихся изъ пламени пещной, которую тако возопѣли: „Благословите вся дѣла Господня Господа пойте и превозносите Его въ вѣки“. ι) Пѣснь IX-ая взята есть изъ Евангеліа св. Луки гл. I. ст. 68—79., которую возопѣлъ пророковъ Захаріа, Отецъ Іоанна Крестит., когда породился его сынъ, тако: „Благословенъ Господь Богъ Израилевъ“ и проч. Въ началѣ сей 9-ой пѣсни находится и пѣснь Богородицы оу Луки гл. I. ст. 46., которую она носивше въ чревѣ своемъ Спасителя тако возопѣла: „Величитъ душа моя Господа и возрадовася духъ мой о Бозѣ Спасѣ моемъ“. — Сіи пѣсни Мойсеевы суть дуже важны, они бо канонамъ службы воскресной суть основа. — Теперь лишь въ великомъ постѣ передъ пѣснями канона читаются. Кромѣ сего пѣснь I-ая и VIII-ая еще въ вел. Субботу на Вечерни межи 15 париміями на красною vпофонію поется. Далѣе нужно замѣтити, что когда еще въ Христовой церкви не было канона воскреснаго, вѣроятно сіи пѣсни оупотреблялися.
units.english_text: 8. **A Verse** [*Stikh*] (in Greek: *stichos* [στίχος] == *versiculus*) is a short chant, taken either from the psalms, or from the Holy Scripture of the New or Old Testament, proclaimed before the stichera according to the melody of the stichera. Verses are either taken, or given [prescribed], or antiphonal. (α) Taken verses are verses from the evening psalms at “Lord, I have cried” and from the psalms at the Praises [Lauds] at Matins and from the Beatitudes of Jesus Christ;[^48] (β) Given verses are according to the dogmatic significance of the feasts and rites at Vespers, at the aposticha, at Compline, at the Litiya, at Matins at the aposticha, and at the Royal Hours, and on various occasions;[^49] (γ) Besides these there are also antiphonal verses, of which the most renowned are those verses which are sung at Matins after the Polyeleos at the exaltations [megalynaria], where after the verses there is for the most part the refrain “We magnify thee,” furthermore at “My soul doth magnify the Lord,” where “More honorable than the Cherubim” is sung, or at the Liturgy at the antiphons, where after the verses “By the prayers of the Mother of God” or “Save us, O Son of God” is repeated.

units.slavonic_incipit: стихиры. Стихи суть либо взяты, либо
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: стихиры стихи сут либо взяты либо данны либо
units.slavonic_text: стихиры. Стихи суть либо взяты, либо данны, либо антифональны. α) Взяты суть стихи изъ псалмовъ вечерныхъ „Господи воззвахъ“ и изъ псалмовъ „Хвалите на Оутрени и изъ блаженствахъ Іисуса Христа“*) β) Данны же суть по догматическомъ значенію праздниковъ и обрядовъ на вечерни, на стиховнѣхъ, на повечеріи, на литіи, на оутрени на стиховнѣхъ и на часахъ царскихъ и по разнымъ случаямъ.**) γ) Кромѣ сего суть еще стихи антифональныи, изъ которыхъ знаменитнѣйшіи суть тѣ стихи, которіи на Оутрени по полуелею на величаніяхъ, гдѣ по стихамъ по большей части припѣвъ „Величаемъ тя“, далѣе на „Величитъ душа моя“, гдѣ „Честнѣйшую Херувимъ“, либо на Литургіи на антифонахъ, гдѣ по стихамъ „Молитвами Богородицы“ или „Спаси насъ Сыне Божій“ повторяется.
units.english_text: 9. **The Prokimenon** (in Greek: *prokeimenon distichon* [προκείμενον δίσтиχον] == *praevium distichon*, from the word *prokeimai* [πρόκειμαι] == *propositus sum vel positus sum ante*) is a two-fold verse, which is taken for the most part from the psalms, and is set forth before the reading of Holy Scripture and remindeth the faithful of Holy Scripture, or of some extraordinary chant, the subject of which it containeth within itself in brief (*complexive*). Prokimena regarding their usage are: (α) Vespers prokimena, which are used at Vespers both great and small; (β) Matins prokimena, which are taken only at great Matins; (γ) Liturgical prokimena, which are used at Liturgies; (δ) Finally, prokimena according to various services and needs. — Both movable and immovable feasts have their proper prokimena. Nevertheless, of the prokimena prescribed for movable feasts the most renowned are: the daily prokimena used at Vespers throughout the entire week;[^50] furthermore the Sunday prokimena sung at Matins according to the 8 tones, and the Sunday prokimena used at Liturgies according to the 8 tones.[^51] — If in the church books at evening divine services we find this phrase: “Prokimenon of the day” (*prokeimenon tes hemeras* [προκείμενον τῆς ἡμέρας]), then under this we always understand the movable day, that is, Monday, Tuesday, etc., whose prokimenon we take. As regards melody, prokimena are divided into: (α) Great, and (β) Small. Great prokimena are sung with a longer melody, while small ones are sung with a shorter melody.

units.slavonic_incipit: новъ на праздники движимыи предписанныхъ знаменитнѣйшіи
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: нов на праздники движимыи предписанных знаменитнейшии сут прокимени
units.slavonic_text: новъ на праздники движимыи предписанныхъ знаменитнѣйшіи суть: прокимени дневніи на Вечерняхъ всея седмицы оупотребляемыи;*) далѣе прокимени недѣльніи на Оутрени поемыи по 8 гласамъ, и прокимени недѣльніи на Литургіяхъ по 8 гласамъ оупотребляемыи.**) — Если въ книгахъ церковныхъ на вечерныхъ богослуженіяхъ найдемъ сіе слово „прокименъ дню“ (προκείμενον τῆς ἡμέρας) то разумѣемъ подъ симъ всегда день движимый, т. е. Понедѣлокъ, Вторникъ и пр., егоже прокименъ беремъ. Касательно же мелодіи прокимены раздѣляются на α) великіи, β) на малыи. Великіи съ долгшею мелодіею, малыи же съ коротшею мелодіею спѣваются.
units.english_text: 10. **Stichera** (in Greek: *sticheron* [стиχηρὸν] == *versus*) are strophes of a single poem composed according to dogmatic significance or according to the propriety of the feast, before which a short verse is sung, and that in such wise that the subject of this verse is explained, amplified, or interpreted in the sticheron. Stichera according to liturgical usage are stichera: (α) At Vespers at “Lord, I have cried” and at the Aposticha; (β) At Compline; (γ) At the Litiya; (δ) At Matins at the Praises [Lauds] and at the Aposticha; (ε) At the Royal Hours; and (ϛ) At the Typika [Obyednytsia]. As regards melody they are sung according to the 8 tones, and the tones of the stichera are designated in the church books. Of stichera according to their dogmatic significance the most renowned are: (α) Resurrectional (*anastasima* [ἀναστάσιμα]), in which the Resurrection of Christ is glorified; (β) Cross-resurrectional (*stauroanastasima* [σταυροαναστάσιма]), in which the Cross and Resurrection of Christ are glorified; (γ) Triadica (*triadika* [тριαδικὰ]), composed in honor of the Holy Trinity; (δ) Theotokia (*theotokia* [θεοτόκια]), composed in honor of the Most Holy Theotokos; (ε) Stavrotheotokia (*staurotheotokia* [σταυροθεοτόκια]), in honor of the compassions [sorrows] of the Mother of God; (ϛ) Martyria (*martyrika* [μαρτυρικὰ]), composed in honor of the holy martyrs; (η) Stichera of Pascha, composed in honor of the Feast of Pascha; (ϑ) Stichera of the departed (*nekrosima* [νεκρώσιма]), wherein supplications are set forth for the deceased; (ι) Eastern stichera (*anatolika* [ἀνατολικὰ]), which it is necessary to chant before the rising of the sun. (κ) Besides these, most especially worthy of note are the so-called “Evangelical Stichera,” of which there are 11 and which are sung at Sunday Matins (at the Praises [Lauds], and that at “Glory”), and which are composed according to the 11 Matins Gospels, being in union with them as regards their subject matter.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 11 самогласна по гречески ест таковая стихира
units.slavonic_text: 11. „Самогласна“ (по гречески: „ἰδιόμελον“) есть таковая стихира, которая не спѣвалася по мелодіи ни тропаря, ни ірмоса, но свою собственную и поважную мелодію имѣла (ἴδιον ἔχον μέλος) и прото не спѣвалася съ стихомъ, но безъ него. Изъ самогласныхъ стихиръ знаменитнѣйшія суть тѣ, которыхъ мелодію на 8 гласовъ вѣроятно первый разъ въ Болгаріи найшли и прото назвали ихъ „Болгар“-ами. 12. „Подобны“ т. е. стихиры (στιχηρὰ προσόμοια) суть таковыя первоначальныя стихиры, на подобіе которыхъ и иныя стихиры суть метрично составленны и по которыхъ мелодіи и другія поются. 13. Тропарь (по гречески: „τροπάριον“.) Нѣкоторые сіе имя производятъ отъ текста, а другіи отъ мелодіи. Изъ тѣхъ, которіи тое имя отъ текста т. е. по значеніи толкуютъ, суть, которіи производятъ сіе имя отъ греческаго слова: „τρόπος“ == способъ житія (modus vivendi), ибо въ тропарахъ содержится образъ житія святаго, либо описаніе праздника. Другіи же производятъ отъ греч. слова: „τρόπαιος“ == знакъ побѣды (signum victoriae), понеже въ тропарахъ прославляется побѣда святаго, либо торжество праздника. Иныи же вновь производятъ тое въ перенесенномъ смыслѣ отъ слова: „τρόπος“ == образъ (imago, figura), и то прото, ибо въ тропарахъ представляется святый подъ различными образами, какъ: лучъ, звѣзда и т. д. А на послѣдъ нѣкоторыи отъ слова: „τρέπειν“ == обращатися, (vertere), понеже тропарь имѣетъ вѣрныхъ на такій животъ наклонити, какій намъ въ тропарахъ представляется. Тѣ же, которіи по мелодіи толкуютъ, производятъ, такожде отъ „τρέπειν“ == обращатися, понеже тѣ поемы касательно мелодіи на различныи образы т. е. на гласы, на подобны, и на иныи образы обращаются. Впрочемъ тропари суть либо короткіи гимны, либо строфы одной долгшой поемы, которыи безъ сопровожденіа музыки въ церкви пѣли. И семъ сходно, они раздѣляются на двѣ части, на „самостоятельныи“ и на „подчиненныи“. 1) Тропарь какъ самостоятельный, есть короткій гимнъ въ церкви спѣваемый, въ которомъ выражается существенность дня, праздника, намѣреніа или описуется добродѣтелями полная жизнь святаго. Можно также въ семъ смыслѣ тропарь назвати и пѣніемъ головнымъ или оуправляющимъ (canticum principale vel regens). Тропари самостоятельныи имѣютъ 8 мелодій (гласовъ), и одинъ тропарь лишь одну, а не два мелодіи имѣетъ, въ которой нужно всякій разъ обращатися, колькоразъ тропарь поется. Тропари самостоятель-
units.english_text: 11. **An Automelon [Idiomelon]** (in Greek: *idiomelon* [ἰδιόμελον]) is such a sticheron that was not chanted according to the melody of either a troparion or a heirmos, but had its own proper and solemn melody (*idion echon melon* [ἴδιον ἔχον μέλος]), and therefore was not chanted with a verse, but without it. Of the automela [idiomela] the most renowned are those whose melody in the 8 tones was probably found for the first time in Bulgaria, and therefore they called them “Bulgarian” [*Bolgar*] chants.

units.slavonic_text: 11. „Самогласна“ (по гречески: „ἰδιόμελον“) есть таковая стихира, которая не спѣвалася по мелодіи ни тропаря, ни ірмоса, но свою собственную и поважную мелодію имѣла (ἴδιον ἔχον μέλος) и прото не спѣвалася съ стихомъ, но безъ него. Изъ самогласныхъ стихиръ знаменитнѣйшія суть тѣ, которыхъ мелодію на 8 гласовъ вѣроятно первый разъ въ Болгаріи найшли и прото назвали ихъ „Болгар“-ами. 12. „Подобны“ т. е. стихиры (στιχηρὰ προσόμοια) суть таковыя первоначальныя стихиры, на подобіе которыхъ и иныя стихиры суть метрично составленны и по которыхъ мелодіи и другія поются. 13. Тропарь (по гречески: „τροπάριον“.) Нѣкоторые сіе имя производятъ отъ текста, а другіи отъ мелодіи. Изъ тѣхъ, которіи тое имя отъ текста т. е. по значеніи толкуютъ, суть, которіи производятъ сіе имя отъ греческаго слова: „τρόπος“ == способъ житія (modus vivendi), ибо въ тропарахъ содержится образъ житія святаго, либо описаніе праздника. Другіи же производятъ отъ греч. слова: „τρόπαιος“ == знакъ побѣды (signum victoriae), понеже въ тропарахъ прославляется побѣда святаго, либо торжество праздника. Иныи же вновь производятъ тое въ перенесенномъ смыслѣ отъ слова: „τρόπος“ == образъ (imago, figura), и то прото, ибо въ тропарахъ представляется святый подъ различными образами, какъ: лучъ, звѣзда и т. д. А на послѣдъ нѣкоторыи отъ слова: „τρέπειν“ == обращатися, (vertere), понеже тропарь имѣетъ вѣрныхъ на такій животъ наклонити, какій намъ въ тропарахъ представляется. Тѣ же, которіи по мелодіи толкуютъ, производятъ, такожде отъ „τρέπειν“ == обращатися, понеже тѣ поемы касательно мелодіи на различныи образы т. е. на гласы, на подобны, и на иныи образы обращаются. Впрочемъ тропари суть либо короткіи гимны, либо строфы одной долгшой поемы, которыи безъ сопровожденіа музыки въ церкви пѣли. И семъ сходно, они раздѣляются на двѣ части, на „самостоятельныи“ и на „подчиненныи“. 1) Тропарь какъ самостоятельный, есть короткій гимнъ въ церкви спѣваемый, въ которомъ выражается существенность дня, праздника, намѣреніа или описуется добродѣтелями полная жизнь святаго. Можно также въ семъ смыслѣ тропарь назвати и пѣніемъ головнымъ или оуправляющимъ (canticum principale vel regens). Тропари самостоятельныи имѣютъ 8 мелодій (гласовъ), и одинъ тропарь лишь одну, а не два мелодіи имѣетъ, въ которой нужно всякій разъ обращатися, колькоразъ тропарь поется. Тропари самостоятель-

units.english_text: 13. **A Troparion** (in Greek: *troparion* [троπάριον]). Some derive this name from the text, and others from the melody. Of those who explain that name from the text, that is, according to its meaning, there are some who derive this name from the Greek word *tropos* [τρόπος] == a manner of living (*modus vivendi*), for in troparia is contained the manner of life of a saint, or a description of the feast. Others again derive it from the Greek word *tropaios* [τρόπαιος] == a trophy of victory (*signum victoriae*), because in troparia the victory of a saint is glorified, or the triumph of a feast. Others again derive it in a metaphorical sense from the word *tropos* [τρόπος] == an image (*imago, figura*), and that because in troparia a saint is represented under various figures, such as: a ray, a star, etc. And finally, some derive it from the word *trepein* [тρέπειν] == to turn (*vertere*), because a troparion hath the aim to incline the faithful unto such a life as is represented to us in troparia. Those who explain it according to melody likewise derive it from *trepein* [тρέπειν] == to turn, because those poems with respect to melody are turned in various manners, that is, unto the tones, unto prosomoia, and unto other models. Moreover, troparia are either short hymns or strophes of a single long poem which they sang in church without accompaniment of music. And according to this, they are divided into two parts, into “independent” and into “subordinate.” 1) A troparion as independent is a short hymn chanted in church, wherein is expressed the essence of the day, of the feast, or of the intention, or the virtue-filled life of a saint is described. One may also in this sense call a troparion a principal or ruling chant (*canticum principale vel regens*). Independent troparia have 8 melodies (tones), and a single troparion hath only one, and not two melodies, unto which it is necessary each time to turn, as many times as the troparion is sung. Independent troparia are given both on movable feasts and on immovable feasts, both on Sundays and on weekdays; besides this, diverse intentions also have their proper troparia. Of troparia the most renowned are: the 8 Sunday troparia in the 8 tones chanted throughout 8 weeks. Every single troparion is joined with a Theotokion troparion, because according to the custom accepted in the Greek Church we at all prayers magnify the Mother of God and entrust ourselves unto her mighty intercession. Besides this, independent troparia are joined with a kontakion, an ikos, a synaxarion, and with a hypakoe.

Единокаждый тропарь совокупленъ есть съ тропаремъ Богородичнымъ, понеже по принятому въ греческ. церкви обычаю мы при всѣхъ молитвахъ величаемъ Матерь Божію и вручаемся ей могущему ходатайству. units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 14 кондак по гречески от
units.slavonic_text: 14. Кондакъ (по гречески: „κοντάκιον“ == breviculum отъ κοντὸς == brevis). Такъ называется или отъ текста, ибо есть короткій гимнъ (hymnus brevis), или отъ мелодіи (ἐν κοντῷ == breviter), ибо его нужно было въ короткой мелодіи (brevis modulus) спѣвати. Кондаки въ союзѣ суть съ тропарями самостоятельными и для выполненіа мыслей въ тропарахъ сложенныхъ служатъ. 15. Икосъ (по гречески: „οἶκος“ == domus vel imago) есть гимнъ въ церкви спѣваемый, который славу и значеніе праздника или похвалу святаго обширнѣйше якъ кондакъ и въ образахъ выражаетъ. Икосъ противоположенъ есть кондаку, кондакъ бо въ кратцѣ, ікосъ же въ своей полнотѣ (amplius et diffusius) описуетъ намъ праздникъ. Ікосъ всегда послѣ кондака слѣдуетъ и никогда безъ кондака не читается.

units.english_text: 14. **A Kontakion** (in Greek: *kontakion* [κοντάкιον] == *breviculum*, from *kontos* [κονтὸς] == *brevis*). Kontakia are in union with independent troparia and serve for the fulfillment of the thoughts composed in troparia.

An ikos always followeth after a kontakion and is never read without a kontakion.

units.slavonic_text: 16. Ѵпакой (по гречески: „ὑπακοὴ“, отъ слова: „ὑπακούω“ == внимати, слышати, aures praebere ad audiendum verbum vel respondere) есть оудивленія достойный гимнъ (по гречески: „ᾠδιον θαυμαστὸν“), который когда спѣвалъ діаконъ самогласно, всѣ людіе его съ богобойною тихостію слѹхали, но дрѹгіи еще и то кажѹтъ, что лишь половинѹ спѣвалъ діаконъ, а половинѹ народъ. Недѣли по 8 гласамъ, далѣе еще и нѣкоторыи праздники имѣютъ свой ѵпакой, но который теперь оу насъ токмо читается на оутреняхъ по сѣдальныхъ и на малыхъ повечеріяхъ. Ѵпакой, хотя поставляется на мѣстѣ сѣдальныхъ, когда сидѣти позволяетса, однакожъ онъ стоячи пѣти и слышатися имѣетъ.
units.english_text: 16. **Hypakoe** (in Greek: *hypakoe* [ὑπακοὴ], from the word *hypakouo* [ὑπακούω] == to give heed, to hear, *aures praebere ad audiendum verbum vel respondere*) is a hymn worthy of wonder (in Greek: *oidion thaumaston* [ᾠδιον θαυμαστὸν]), which when the deacon chanted as an idiomelon (lit. 'samohlasno'), all the people listened unto it with God-fearing quietude; yet others say also that the deacon chanted only half, and the people half. The Sundays according to the 8 tones, and furthermore also certain feasts, have their proper hypakoe, which now among us is only read at Matins after the sessional hymns and at Little Compline. The hypakoe, although it is appointed in the place of the sessional hymns, when it is permitted to sit, nevertheless is to be sung and heard while standing.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 17 канон от греческаго слова
units.slavonic_text: 17. Канонъ (отъ греческаго слова: „κανών“ == regula) вообще есть найдолгшая поема церковная по опредѣленному ряду составленная, состоящая изъ 9 пѣсней. Прото состоитъ канонъ изъ 9 пѣсней, чтобы тѣми оуподобитися людямъ 9 хорамъ ангелскимъ, которіи Бога непрестанно прославляютъ. Раздѣляется же канонъ малыми ектеніами и иными пѣніями на три головныи отдѣлы въ честь трехъ головныхъ чиновъ*) ангелскихъ, и то такъ, что по 3-ой пѣсни берется „сѣдаленъ“, по 6-ой „кондакъ“ и „ікосъ“, а по 9-ой „свѣтиленъ“. Каноны же по своему догматическому значенію сѹть: α) воскресныи (ἀναστάσιμοι), β) крестныи (σταυρόσιμοι), γ) крестовоскресныи (σταυροαναστάσιμοι), δ) тройчніи (τριάδικοι), ε) богородичніи (θεοτόκιοι), ζ) крестобогородичніи (σταυροθεοτόκιοι), η) догматическіи (δογμάτικοι), ι) о оусопшихъ (νεκρόσιμοι), κ) молебныи (ἱκετήριοι) и различныи по праздникамъ Господскимъ, Богородичнымъ и Святыхъ.
units.english_text: 17. **Canon** (from the Greek word *kanon* [κανών] == *regula*) in general is the longest church poem composed according to a determined order, consisting of 9 odes. A canon consisteth of 9 odes for this reason, namely, that by them men may be likened unto the 9 angelic choirs, who unceasingly glorify God. The canon is divided by little ektenias and other chants into three chief sections in honor of the three chief orders[^54] of angels, and that in such wise that after the 3rd Ode a “sessional hymn” is taken, after the 6th a “kontakion” and “ikos,” and after the 9th the “Exaposteilarion.” Canons according to their dogmatic significance are: (α) Resurrectional (*anastasimoi* [ἀναστάσιμοι]), (β) Cross (*staurosimoi* [σταυρόσιμοι]), (γ) Cross-resurrectional (*stauroanastasimoi* [σταυροαναστάσιμοι]), (δ) Triadica (*triadikoi* [τριάδικοι]), (ε) Theotokia (*theotokioi* [θεοτόκιοι]), (ϛ) Cross-Theotokia (*staurotheotokioi* [σταυροθεοτόκιοι]), (η) Dogmatic (*dogmatikoi* [δογμάτικοι]), (ϑ) Of the departed (*nekrosimoi* [νекρόσιμοι]), (ι) Supplicatory (*hiketerioi* [ἱκετήριοι]), and diverse ones according to Feasts of the Lord, of the Mother of God, and of Saints.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 18 песн по гречески ест част канона
units.slavonic_text: 18. Пѣснь (по гречески: „ᾠδὴ“) есть часть канона и она есть долгшая поема состоящая изъ больше себѣ подобныхъ тропарей, (т. е. строфокъ) и спѣванная живымъ голосомъ, а не посредствомъ нѣкихъ мѹзикальныхъ орѹдій. Первый тропарь пѣсни называется „Ірмос“-омъ, и передъ нимъ не поется припѣвъ, передъ 2-ымъ и 3-имъ поется припѣвъ, и пр., передъ пред-послѣднымъ тропаремъ поется „Слава“, а передъ послѣднымъ „И нынѣ“. Заключительный же тропарь называется „Катавасіею“; и передъ нимъ такжеде не поется припѣвъ.
units.english_text: 18. **An Ode** (in Greek: *oide* [ᾠδὴ]) is a part of a canon and is a longer poem consisting of several troparia similar to one another (that is, strophes) and chanted with a living voice, and not by means of any musical instruments. The first troparion of an ode is called the “Heirmos,” and before it a refrain is not sung; before the 2nd and 3rd a refrain is sung, etc.; before the penultimate troparion “Glory” is sung, and before the last “Now and.” The concluding troparion is called the “Katavasia”; and before it likewise a refrain is not sung.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 19 ирмос по гречески связ
units.slavonic_text: 19. Ірмосъ (по гречески: „εἱρμός“ == tractus связъ) есть первый тропарь пѣсни, который въ себѣ самостоятельный есть такъ метричнаго составленія, какъ и мелодійнаго спѣванія, но касательно прочихъ слѣдѹемыхъ тропарей связательную задачѹ
units.english_text: 19. **The Heirmos** (in Greek: *heirmos* [εἱρμός] == *tractus*, a link or connection) is the first troparion of an ode, which is independent in itself both in metrical composition and in melodic chanting, but with respect unto the other subsequent troparia it hath a connective function.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 20 припев ест стих который перед тропарями ирмосу
units.slavonic_text: 20. Припѣвъ есть стихъ, который передъ тропарями ірмосѹ подчиненными поется. Припѣвъ по догматическомѹ значенію пѣсни есть различный. Сѹть припѣквы: α) Воскресныи, на пр. „Слава Господи святомѹ воскресенію Твоемѹ!“ β) Крестовоскресныи, на пр. „Слава Господи крестѹ и воскресенію Твоемѹ!“ γ) Богородичныи, на пр. „Пресвятая Госпоже Богородице спаси насъ!“ δ) Святымъ Апостоламъ на пр. „Св. Апостоле Христовъ, моли Бога о насъ“. ε) Св. Отцамъ, на пр. „Святителю Отче, моли Бога о насъ“. η) Преподобнымъ Отцамъ, на пр. „Св. Преподобный Отче, моли Бога о насъ“. ζ) Преподобнымъ женамъ, на пр. „Преподобная Мати, моли Бога о насъ!“ ϑ) Мѹченикамъ, на пр. „Св. Мѹчениче, моли Бога о насъ!“ и пр.
units.english_text: 20. **A Refrain** [*Pripiv*] is a verse which is sung before the troparia subordinate unto the heirmos. The refrain is diverse according to the dogmatic significance of the ode. There are refrains: (α) Resurrectional, for example: “Glory, O Lord, to Thy holy resurrection!”; (β) Cross-resurrectional, for example: “Glory, O Lord, to Thy cross and resurrection!”; (γ) Theotokia, for example: “Most Holy Lady Theotokos, save us!”; (δ) Unto the Holy Apostles, for example: “Holy Apostle of Christ, pray unto God for us”; (ε) Unto Holy Hierarchs, for example: “Holy Father and Hierarch, pray unto God for us”; (ϛ) Unto Venerable Fathers, for example: “Holy Venerable Father, pray unto God for us”; (η) Unto Venerable Women, for example: “Venerable Mother, pray unto God for us!”; (ϑ) Unto Martyrs, for example: “Holy Martyr, pray unto God for us!” etc.

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: 21 катавасиа от греческаго слова снисхождение
units.slavonic_text: 21. Катавасіа (отъ греческаго слова: „καταβαίνω“ == снисхожденіе) есть послѣдный тропарь пѣсни, который когда спѣвали, оба хоры выходили на серединѹ церкви, и тамъ пропѣли сей тропарь. Катавасіа есть или: α) порадочная, сирѣчь она есть самъ ірмосъ, который на концѣ пѣсни повторяется, или есть: β) рядовая, т. е. на нѣкій часъ опредѣленна и тая есть ірмосы праздничныхъ каноновъ. На пр. катавасіа рядовая по отданію Воздвиженіа ч. Креста до 21-го Ноября: „Отверзѹ оуста моя“, отъ 21-го Нояб. до 1-го Янв. есть „Христосъ раждается“.
units.english_text: 21. **Katavasia** (from the Greek word *katabaino* [καταβαίνω] == descent) is the last troparion of an ode, which when they chanted, both choirs came forth into the midst of the church, and there sang this troparion. A katavasia is either: (α) Ordinary, that is, it is the heirmos itself repeated at the end of the ode; or (β) Prescribed, that is, appointed for a certain season, and such are the heirmoi of festal canons. For example, the prescribed katavasia after the Apodosis of the Exaltation of the Precious Cross until November 21 is: “I shall open my mouth”; from November 21 until January 1 it is: “Christ is born.”
